data.summary: F10 stoppages are driven mainly by part shortages and AGV delays, with secondary torque faults on M-06; andon and telemetry data confirm missing_part, equipment faults, and machine failures contribute to repeated line stops.

findings.claim: Part shortages are the largest downtime driver at F10: supplier_short (high) has 22 incidents and 459.0 min downtime, and agv_down (medium) has 58 incidents and 171.9 min downtime.
Torque faults recur heavily at F10: controller_fault (medium) has 36 incidents and 451.7 min downtime, and torque_out_of_range (medium) has 37 incidents and 186.5 min downtime.
Andon events show missing_part is a top line-stop trigger at F10: 97 stopped_line events in shift A averaging 186.3 s response, plus 60 stopped_line events in shift B.
Equipment andon events also stop the F10 line in both shifts: 65 events in shift A and 66 events in shift B with stopped_line=true.
Machine telemetry at F10 logs 47 failure rows on M-06, with overstrain_failure sometimes equal to 1 and torque up to 76.6 nm, while heat_dissipation_failure remains 0.

data.recommendation: Focus first on supplier_short part shortages and AGV delays at F10, then inspect the M-06 torque controller and socket wear, because these causes produce the most downtime and stopped-line andon events.
